name: GlzTable
semanticRole: Present comparable structured data with explicit column relationships, sorting, resizing, selection, and keyboard navigation.

material.rule: Data cells and headers are solid readability surfaces. Glaze is not a default table-cell material; only separate floating table chrome may use it.

input.keyboard: Supports deterministic cell or row navigation, sortable header activation, selection, and access to row actions without requiring pointer hover.
input.focus: Focused cell, row, header, and resize handle have explicit visible focus independent from selected state.
input.hover: Row hover uses restrained tint and may expose secondary actions; it never hides data required for comparison.
input.press: Press selects or activates only according to the table's declared interaction mode and gives immediate feedback.
input.selection: Selected rows use tint plus checkbox or indicator and preserve readable data contrast.
input.directManipulation: Column resize exposes a visible 1px divider with an approximately 8–12px hit region; resize and reorder operations preserve headers and avoid viewport overflow.

accessibility.role: Use native table semantics for static data and the appropriate grid pattern only when cell-level interaction requires it.
accessibility.name: The table has an accessible caption or programmatic name when surrounding context does not already provide one.
accessibility.state: Sort direction, selection, disabled controls, loading, error, and resize/reorder state are exposed when applicable.
accessibility.value: Cell text/value and sortable header state remain programmatically available; no visual-only data encoding is permitted.
accessibility.keyboard: Sorting, selection, row actions, resize alternatives, and grid navigation are keyboard operable according to the chosen semantic pattern.
accessibility.focus: Focus is visible on the active cell/row/header/handle independently from selection.
accessibility.errorAssociation: Loading and error states are associated with the table region and do not replace headings needed to understand recovery.
accessibility.reducedMotion: Resize/reorder/selection feedback becomes direct without animated data movement when reduced motion is active.
accessibility.reducedTransparency: Table cells remain opaque; any floating chrome resolves to opaque Raised material.
accessibility.increasedContrast: Strengthen row, focus, sort, selection, and resize indicators.
accessibility.forcedColors: Use system colors while retaining sort arrows, checkmarks, focus, and explicit status text.
accessibility.largeText: Rows grow and columns scroll or transform without overlapping values or controls.

fallbacks.reducedMotion: Use direct resize, sort, selection, and reorder feedback.
fallbacks.reducedTransparency: Keep data cells opaque and floating chrome solid.
fallbacks.highContrast: Strengthen grid boundaries only where needed plus focus, sort, and selection cues.
fallbacks.forcedColors: Use system colors and structural indicators.
fallbacks.performance: Remove decorative effects and virtualize large datasets before weakening table semantics.

content.overflow: Wide tables scroll within their owned region or transform to an explicitly documented mobile representation; they must not force page-level horizontal overflow.
content.localization: Headers, values, sort labels, number/date formats, and status text tolerate expansion and locale formatting.
content.rtl: Column order follows product semantics and direction policy; resize and sort affordances mirror logically while numbers and intrinsic-direction identifiers remain intact.

criteria: Headers remain visually subordinate to data while preserving strong column association.
Sort direction, row selection, keyboard focus, and hover are independently legible.
Resize hit regions are forgiving without visually thick dividers.
Dense datasets remain solid and readable rather than turning cells into repeated glass surfaces.
